target_customer: Consumer packaged goods manufacturers (who fund the discounts) and grocery retailers; shoppers redeem the offers
problem: Printed grocery coupons are wasteful and hard to target. Aisle50 let shoppers prepay for a manufacturer deal online and load it onto their store loyalty card.
business_model: Manufacturer-paid deals: the manufacturer covers the discount, Aisle50's cut and an 8 cent handling fee to the retailer
product_category: Digital grocery deals and CPG marketing

founders.name: Riley Scott
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; background not found.

founders.name: George Korsnick
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as CTO; background not found.

competitors.name: Groupon
competitors.what: Daily deals; TechCrunch (2012) framed Aisle50 as a Groupon for groceries but with manufacturer-funded deals

competitors.name: Cellfire
competitors.what: Digital grocery coupons loaded to the shopper loyalty card
competitors.traction_then: Retailer rollouts such as ShopRite; dated detail not verified

technical_complexity.rationale: Required integrating with retailer loyalty card systems and point of sale redemption, plus payments and offer logistics; the engineering was standard but integrations were slow.

defensibility.rationale: Retailer integrations and manufacturer relationships helped, but coupon players like Cellfire and Coupons.com already had similar ties.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The YC directory lists Aisle50 as acquired; the acquirer and date were not confirmed by a reliable source.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2012) reported 26% of redeemers had not shopped at the store in over a month and 50% bought the product for the first time, evidence that manufacturers wanted trial.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; search results were swamped by similarly named companies (Aisle411, Aisles, Aisle Planner).

outcome_analysis: Aisle50 raised $2.6M in January 2012 after launching with Lowes Foods in August 2011 and early data showing it brought lapsed and new product buyers. The YC directory lists it as acquired, but the acquirer, date and price were not confirmed by a reliable source, so the strength of the outcome is unknown.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503. Aggregators disagree: CB Insights says about $5.22M total and a $2.6M Series A-II in August 2013; Dealroom says a $2.6M Series A in August 2013 led by Origin Ventures and an acquisition by Groupon in February 2015. These are unverified and not recorded. Round stage left as other since TechCrunch did not label it in the text I read. Founding year not stated by a source I opened (sources conflict on launch 2010 vs 2012). Competition list rests on a later TechCrunch comparison and a 2010 GfK piece, not dated 2011 competitor coverage.
